subject: Phase 100090: Shared Continuous EMA Update Engine
verdict_justification: The Phase 100090 implementation successfully delivers the shared continuous EMA and trend engine, durable definition-time update_rule declarations with epistemic_kind column separation, dual-backend persistence (SQLite and Postgres) with serializable concurrency, and the generic update rule splitter. All workspace test suites and the >=90% per-file line/function coverage gate pass cleanly. Five non-blocking findings were identified: an addressability mismatch in the update facade, header boundary compliance, discarded discrete new_value, empty-window recovery bypass, and unparameterized SQL LIMIT in SQLite. Remediation r1 addressed all five: F-02/F-04/F-05 fixed in code, F-03 resolved by documenting the gated-write contract, and F-01 resolved by documenting the addressability model as intentional/deterministic with both structural alternatives rejected with reasons; make check and make coverage both pass afterward.

findings.title: Inconsistent addressability between continuous and discrete update paths in update facade
findings.status: Resolved (documented intent; both structural alternatives rejected with reasons)
findings.recommendation: Standardize target addressability across both paths; either allow discrete updates to accept attribute keys and look up current open items, or enable items to reference their declared attr_key so caller update_rule can be validated against item attribute schema.
findings.resolution: Resolved by documenting the addressability contract as intentional and making it deterministic, then rejecting both structural alternatives with reasons. `update_rule` scopes the target namespace (continuous → declared attribute key; discrete → item id), attribute lookup wins over an item-id collision, and the declared-discrete-key-on-discrete-path case now returns a structured `InvalidArgument` that explains the ambiguity (update.rs:98-100,118-150,193-201). A dedicated contract test pins the resolution order and rejection (clio-write::update_tests::t_addressability_precedence_and_discrete_key_rejection). Option 1 (accept attribute keys on the discrete path and look up open items) is unsafe as specified: `update` carries no subject and an attribute key is a bank-wide predicate, so invalidating "by key" would close every subject's open edge; doing it safely needs an API change (add subject) = public-contract change outside Phase 100090 scope. Option 2 (items carry a declared attr_key) is a Phase 100030/100040/100080 schema and write-path change, also outside Phase 100090 scope.

findings.recommendation: Add the mandatory '//! Keep this module focused on <responsibility>.' closing line under ## Boundary in all newly created Rust source files.
findings.resolution: Added the mandatory closing line under '## Boundary' in all 6 named files: attribute.rs:23, attribute_map.rs:21, sqlite_attribute.rs:21, postgres_attribute.rs:21, update.rs:23, persona.rs:21.

findings.title: Discrete update routing silently discards new_value
findings.recommendation: Document why new_value cannot be admitted directly on the discrete branch without bypassing Phase 100040 admission gates, or accept an optional replacement ID for gated replacement.
findings.resolution: Documented at the API boundary: `UpdateArgs::new_value` (update.rs:101-107) and the discrete arm of `route_unregistered` (update.rs:217-223) now state that the discrete path only closes the target's bi-temporal interval and deliberately does not admit `new_value`, because doing so would bypass the §4.2–4.4 admission gates every long-term write must pass. Replacement content is written through the normal gated create tools; `invalidate` accepts `replacement_id` directly for explicit linkage. Programmatic replacement was not added here: `update` receives a value, not an id, so accepting a replacement would require changing the public signature (out of scope; Phase 100040 gated-write ownership).

findings.title: parse_window treats empty array '[]' as valid rather than falling back to series reconstruction
findings.recommendation: Update parse_window to return None when the parsed array has zero elements, ensuring an empty window row triggers history rebuild from continuous_observations.
findings.resolution: `parse_window` now returns `None` for an empty array (`if arr.is_empty() || ...`) (attribute_map.rs:97), so a corrupt `[]` window follows the same rebuild-from-`continuous_observations` path as malformed JSON. Both backends consume this shared helper (sqlite_attribute.rs, postgres_attribute.rs), so the fix applies to both. A stored window always has ≥1 state after any applied observation, so `[]` is a corrupt/truncated row, not a valid cold start. Regression assertion added at attribute_map.rs:178 (`parse_window("[]", 3).is_none()`).

findings.title: Unparameterized LIMIT string formatting in sqlite_attribute.rs
findings.recommendation: Parameterize the LIMIT clause as LIMIT ?4 with params![bank_id, attr_key, as_of, capped as i64], matching postgres_attribute.rs.
findings.resolution: `continuous_series_impl` now binds the cap as a positional parameter (`LIMIT ?4` with `params![bank_id, attr_key, as_of, capped]`) instead of `format!`-interpolating it; `capped` is `limit.min(10_000) as i64` (sqlite_attribute.rs:313-329), matching the Postgres `$4` binding.

issues.title: Inconsistent addressability between continuous and discrete update paths in update facade
issues.why_it_matters: The generic update(item_id, new_value, update_rule) entrypoint specified in §4.9.4.A takes target as item_id, but the implementation bifurcates target semantics: for continuous updates, target must be an attr_key; for discrete updates, target must be an item_id. Calling update with an attribute key for discrete updates returns ErrorCode::InvalidArgument ('discrete updates are item-addressed'), while calling update with an item_id for continuous updates fails with WrongUpdateRule.
issues.impact: Callers cannot use a uniform identifier scheme across update rules, and discrete updates on items cannot verify whether the item belongs to a continuous or discrete attribute schema.
issues.proposed_fix: Standardize target addressability across both paths; either allow discrete updates to accept attribute keys and look up current open items, or enable items to reference their declared attr_key so caller update_rule can be validated against item attribute schema.
issues.status: Resolved (documented intent; both structural alternatives rejected with reasons)
issues.resolution: Same fix as F-01: addressability contract documented as intentional and deterministic, and the two structural options rejected (option 1 would over-close every subject's edges because `update` has no subject and attr_key is bank-wide; option 2 is a Phase 100030/100040/100080 schema change). See crates/clio-write/src/update.rs:98-100,118-150,193-201 and test clio-write::update_tests::t_addressability_precedence_and_discrete_key_rejection.

issues.title: Missing boundary focus statement in newly added module headers
issues.why_it_matters: AGENTS.md defines a strict module header template requiring '//! Keep this module focused on <responsibility>.' under the '## Boundary' section. All newly created production modules in clio-types, clio-store, and clio-write omit this closing sentence.
issues.impact: Minor style and governance compliance defect against the repository's AGENTS.md rules.
issues.proposed_fix: Add the mandatory '//! Keep this module focused on <responsibility>.' closing line under ## Boundary in all newly created Rust source files.
issues.resolution: Same fix as F-02: boundary focus line added under '## Boundary' in all 6 files (attribute.rs:23, attribute_map.rs:21, sqlite_attribute.rs:21, postgres_attribute.rs:21, update.rs:23, persona.rs:21).

issues.title: Discrete update routing silently discards new_value
issues.why_it_matters: The update facade takes new_value as an argument. In the continuous path, new_value is parsed into float and smoothed via EMA. In the discrete path, new_value is completely ignored and None is passed as replacement_id to invalidate(). While closing the prior item satisfies invalidation without bypassing Phase 100040 admission gates, discarding new_value silently without error or replacement linkage is unexpected.
issues.impact: Callers passing a new value expecting it to replace the discrete fact will only invalidate the existing fact without creating or linking a replacement.
issues.proposed_fix: Document why new_value cannot be admitted directly on the discrete branch without bypassing Phase 100040 admission gates, or accept an optional replacement ID for gated replacement.
issues.resolution: Same fix as F-03: rationale documented at `UpdateArgs::new_value` (update.rs:101-107) and the discrete arm of `route_unregistered` (update.rs:217-223). Programmatic replacement deferred: `update` carries a value, not an id, so adding replacement linkage would change the public signature (out of Phase 100090 scope; Phase 100040 owns gated writes).

issues.title: parse_window treats empty array '[]' as valid rather than falling back to series reconstruction
issues.why_it_matters: In parse_window, '[]' parses successfully as Some(vec![]). If continuous_state.window_json is corrupted with '[]' while continuous_observations has retained history points, observe_continuous_impl uses an empty prior window instead of triggering rebuild_window_from_points, resetting the EMA to cold start.
issues.impact: A corrupted empty window array causes unnecessary cold-start reset despite available historical observations.
issues.proposed_fix: Update parse_window to return None when the parsed array has zero elements (if window.is_empty() { return None; }), ensuring an empty window row triggers history rebuild from continuous_observations.
issues.resolution: Same fix as F-04: attribute_map.rs:97 returns None for an empty array, routing both backends to rebuild from continuous_observations; regression assertion at attribute_map.rs:178.

issues.title: Unparameterized LIMIT string formatting in sqlite_attribute.rs
issues.why_it_matters: continuous_series_impl in sqlite_attribute.rs formats capped as i64 directly into the SQL string via format!(... LIMIT {}, capped as i64) rather than binding it as a positional parameter LIMIT ?4.
issues.impact: Minor inconsistency with postgres_attribute.rs (which binds $4) and SQL formatting best practices.
issues.proposed_fix: Parameterize the LIMIT clause as LIMIT ?4 with params![bank_id, attr_key, as_of, capped as i64], matching postgres_attribute.rs.
issues.resolution: Same fix as F-05: sqlite_attribute.rs:313-329 binds `LIMIT ?4` with `params![bank_id, attr_key, as_of, capped]`; no string interpolation.

dismissed: Non-encrypted numeric states in continuous_state/continuous_observations: Reviewed against §7.4 and Phase 100090 scope. DEK encryption applies to content-bearing payloads in items, whereas continuous scalar state is structured metadata; compliance erase of continuous series is explicitly scoped to slice 100190.

Postgres hashtext 32-bit advisory lock: Checked for collision impact. A 32-bit advisory lock hash collision only introduces brief lock serialization between different keys; data integrity is maintained by transactional WHERE bank_id AND attr_key clauses.
